newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels offer prisoner swap with army.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels offer prisoner swap with army.

text.p: A group of Sri Lankan servicemen captured by Tamil Tiger rebels said on Friday they have been offered freedom in exchange for guerrillas held by the military.
The 22 prisoners sent a letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, to opposition leader Ranil Wickremasinghe asking him to help secure their release.
Among the 22 is a naval officer captured by the Tigers when they sank his patrol vessel in a suicide attack in late 1994, on the eve of abortive peace talks with the government.

The letter quoted Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebel leaders as saying that the group had proposed to the government a swap of the 22 prisoners in exchange for three guerrillas captured by the military.
The International Committee of the Red Cross, which has been a mediator in previous prisoner exchanges, declined comment.
A military spokesman said he was unaware of the letter or plans to exchange prisoners of war.
Neither Wickremasinghe, former prime minister during the rule of his United National Party, nor the LTTE's overseas spokesmen were immediately available for comment.

The letter said the LTTE wants the release of a rebel identified as "Kennedy" who was captured in an attack on an airbase and two female rebels known as "Mala" and "Uma" captured after a guerrilla attack on a navy base in the north.
The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
